subject: Benchmark methodology & SLO qualification (EdgeFin)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@edgefin.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmark methodology & SLO qualification (EdgeFin) — post-call recap

Hi Jane,

Thanks again for taking the call today — great to meet you and the EdgeFin performance team. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we're aligned: 

Summary of requirements we captured
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 120ms for 512-token generation (streaming enabled)
- Concurrency target: 200 concurrent sessions during peak window
- Throughput: sustained 1.5k requests/minute for inference-heavy endpoints
- Streaming: must support chunked streaming with max initial response time < 60ms
- Reproducibility: benchmark harness must be deterministic across runs and expose seed/config

Proposed next steps
1) We’ll share a draft benchmark methodology and prompt set for your review (attached).
2) EdgeFin to confirm whether we should include your internal prompt variants and any PII-redaction steps.
3) Schedule a 60-minute run-through where we walk through the harness and expected measurements.

Attachments: edgefin-benchmark-specs-v1.pdf (methodology draft), prompt-set-v2.json (example prompts), eval-harness-instructions.md

Can you confirm availability for a run-through next week (June 7 or 8)?

Thanks — happy to sync if you want any changes before the run.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgeFin Performance Team <perf@edgefin.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmark methodology & SLO qualification (EdgeFin) — post-call recap

Hi Marissa,

Appreciate the detailed recap — this looks right. A couple of clarifications from our side before the run-through:

1) Latency SLOs: the 120ms p95 target is for the core model-only path (no heavy post-processing). For endpoints that do reranking we expect p95 up to 200ms — can your harness split those?
2) Concurrency: 200 concurrent *active* streaming sessions (i.e., sessions with open SSE/websocket connections) — our traffic pattern has long-lived streams (~20–40s) during peaks.
3) Throughput: the 1.5k rpm applies to aggregate non-streaming calls. We’ll provide a traffic mix CSV.
4) Reproducibility: we need the harness to expose random seed, batch scheduling, and the sampling/temperature settings used.

We’re available for the run-through on June 7 at 10am PT. Also attaching an internal prompt_variants.csv (not attached here in this thread; will share via Drive link).

Thanks — Jane
Jane Doe
Head of Platform Engineering | EdgeFin
jane.doe@edgefin.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@edgefin.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmark methodology & SLO qualification (EdgeFin) — methodology details

Thanks Jane — that all makes sense. I updated the methodology PDF to call out separate measurement buckets (model-only, model+post-processing/rerank) and included an explicit section on streaming session lifetime and how we measure initial response vs per-chunk latency. Key points in the updated doc: 

- Measurement definitions:
  • Initial response time = time from request acceptance to first byte of model token stream
  • Per-chunk latency = median time between streamed chunks (used for perceived throughput)
  • p95/p99 reported per-bucket and across end-to-end pipeline
- Concurrency accounting: we will emulate long-lived SSE sessions with a background keepalive and record active session counts.
- Throughput: separate non-streaming request generator with configurable ramp and steady-state windows.
- Reproducibility: harness exposes seed, batch_size, pad_strategy, and exact kernel selection logs.

I also added a reproducibility checklist and a small sample run script for us to run on a shared test cluster. See eval-harness-instructions.md.

For the meeting (June 7, 10am PT) agenda I propose:
1) Quick run through the updated methodology and prompts (15m)
2) Demo the harness on a small synthetic workload (20m)
3) Walk the expected metrics and artifacts you’ll receive (10m)
4) Agree on next steps and schedule a larger-scale run (15m)

Let us know if you want to add anything. We’ll also bring Marcus to cover autoscale and capacity planning.

Best,
Marissa

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jane Doe <jane.doe@edgefin.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmark methodology & SLO qualification (EdgeFin) — concurrency and capacity note

Quick note from infra/capacity:

- If EdgeFin expects 200 active streaming sessions with avg stream length of 30s, peak simultaneous token churn could be quite spiky depending on prompt length. We recommend we run a 2-stage scale test: 1) steady-state concurrency validation at 200 active sessions, 2) spike test with bursts up to 400 sessions for 2–5 minutes to validate graceful degradation and fallback rules.
- We’ll capture per-GPU utilization, kernel fallbacks, and queue latency metrics in the artifacts.
- Action: please confirm whether you want to test quantized model variants (we can include q8/q4 runs). That will change the expected latency distribution.

Thanks,
Marcus
Principal Systems Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmark methodology & SLO qualification (EdgeFin) — confirmed and prep

Morning all — thanks for the updates. Confirming the June 7 10am PT run-through. A few prep items from our side:

- We will share the traffic mix CSV and internal prompt_variants.csv in the Drive link you gave this morning.
- Please include quantized (q8) and fp16 runs in the small demo; we expect to evaluate both.
- For spike tests, go ahead and include the 400-session short bursts.
- We also require the harness to output: per-run config JSON, raw token latency traces (timestamped), and a summary CSV with p50/p95/p99 by bucket.

Looking forward to the run-through. Drive links will be live in ~15 minutes.

Best,
Jane
